clue.text: In darkness I lie abandoned, cramped

indicators.note: abandoned suggests letters thrown about wildly, so these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone lies forsaken and confined in the dark.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for being packed tightly together, as fish in a tin, means uncomfortably cramped.

clue.text: Opera singer swapping parts equally divided a venue

indicators.note: the word is cut into two equal halves and the halves change places

parts.note: Maria Callas was a celebrated soprano

explanation.surface: An opera diva swaps roles with a colleague at a performance venue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swapping parts equally divided' turns CAL-LAS into LAS-CAL; add A. The answer is the Milan opera house.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous Milan opera house is a performance venue, given here by its general description.

clue.text: There could be a place for 15 unofficial advisers

definitions.text: There could be a place for 15
definitions.meaning: a kitchen cupboard is where the 15-across blades might be kept
an informal circle of confidants advising a leader outside the official cabinet

explanation.definitionFit: A cupboard in the kitchen houses cutlery; figuratively, a leader's informal group of counsellors.

clue.text: Herb's half-hearted young buck

indicators.note: the herb's central pair of letters loses one of its two, leaving half its heart

explanation.surface: A youthful stag is described as having only a half-hearted interest in herbs.
explanation.walkthrough: SORREL's heart is RR; 'half-hearted' removes one R.
explanation.definitionFit: A sorel is a male fallow deer in its third year, a young buck.

clue.text: European fled, hiding from sultanate

indicators.note: the word for fled conceals the second piece inside it

parts.note: Omani means from Oman, a sultanate in Arabia

explanation.surface: A European escaped and went into hiding from a sultan's realm.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Romania is a European.

clue.text: So lacking purpose, quickly loses strike

indicators.note: loses tells us a piece is taken away from the longer word

explanation.surface: Without aim, someone quickly gives up a strike action.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in an aimless, purposeless manner is doing it idly; 'So' stands for the manner.

clue.text: Honourably placed right on the end, fidgeting

indicators.note: fidgeting means moving restlessly, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone seated in a place of honour fidgets at the very end of the row.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch who is enthroned is ceremonially seated in a place of honour.

clue.text: Turning letters inside and out

parts.note: read 'letters' as things that let people in and out, while turning round

explanation.definitionFit: Rotating entrances at buildings spin round, admitting people in and letting them out.

clue.text: Dramatic team game in cape and short stockings

indicators.note: in places the game inside the other letters
short says the last letter is cut off

parts.note: RU is rugby union, a game

explanation.surface: A team plays its game wearing capes and short stockings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims HOSE to HOS; RU goes into C+HOS.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek drama a group of performers commenting on the action formed the chorus.

clue.text: Chaser of wine and women rested several months

parts.note: YR, a year, is several months

explanation.surface: A rake who chases drink and women takes a long rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A lustful mythical woodland creature, figuratively a lecherous man pursuing pleasure.

clue.text: Child's set to exploit force

parts.note: teeth means force or power, as in a law with teeth

explanation.surface: A child is set up to be exploited by force.
explanation.definitionFit: A child's first set of dentition is lost before the adult set arrives.

clue.text: Pressure with top of hand breaks crooked walking stick

indicators.note: breaks means the other letters are split open to take the insertion
top of means the first letter is taken

explanation.surface: Under pressure, a hand breaks a crooked walking stick.
explanation.definitionFit: A stick cut from an ash sapling is a traditional walking cane.

clue.text: Glade providing shelter for Eliza

indicators.note: Eliza Doolittle of Pygmalion drops her aitches, so the initial letter goes

parts.note: to harbour is to provide shelter

explanation.surface: A woodland clearing offers shelter for a woman called Eliza.
explanation.walkthrough: Eliza Doolittle is the Cockney flower girl of Shaw's Pygmalion, who drops her H's.
explanation.definitionFit: A shady leafy bower in a garden or wood is loosely a glade.

clue.text: Presumably not The Elephant Man as cinema interprets him

indicators.note: interprets suggests rendering in another form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The cinema gives its take on the film The Elephant Man.
explanation.walkthrough: Elephants are said never to forget, so a forgetful person is presumably not one; 'him' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone suffering memory loss is the opposite of an elephant that never forgets.

clue.text: Romantic inscription found round sheltered parking in promenade at night?

indicators.note: found round means the inscription surrounds the other letters

parts.note: SWALK, sealed with a loving kiss, is written on love letters
lee means shelter, the sheltered side

explanation.surface: A love note is found near a sheltered car park on an evening walk.
explanation.walkthrough: SWALK is a British envelope acronym, 'sealed with a loving kiss'.
explanation.definitionFit: Walking while asleep is a whimsical stroll in the night.

clue.text: Weapons, in retrospect, fail to clinch victory in Europe

indicators.note: to clinch means to hold tight, so one piece encloses the other
in retrospect means looking back, so the word is read backwards

explanation.surface: Looking back, weapons failed to secure European victory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in retrospect' turns SINK into KNIS, which holds VE.
explanation.definitionFit: Bladed implements used for stabbing or cutting can serve as arms.

clue.text: Pet wolf's scattered unfortunate lot of chickens

indicators.note: scattered letters are thrown about, so these are rearranged

explanation.surface: A pet wolf scatters an unlucky flock of chickens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scattered' rearranges PETWOLFS; here the S counts.
explanation.definitionFit: An avian disease is the sad fate befalling a flock of poultry.

clue.text: What's in maybe a kerosene container

indicators.note: What's in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A question about what might be in a can of paraffin.
explanation.definitionFit: A glass vessel for laboratory liquids is a kind of receptacle.

clue.text: To British reserve I'd add muscle

parts.note: ice means reserve or cool aloofness
PS, postscript, is what a writer adds

explanation.surface: Someone adds muscle to British reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: The two-headed upper-arm flexor is a well-known muscle.

clue.text: Which sees aged Poles wearing headgear?

definitions.text: Which sees aged Poles wearing headgear?

indicators.note: wearing means the other letters are put on inside the headgear

explanation.surface: Elderly Polish people put on hats when the weather turns.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden spell of chilly weather is when elderly folk wear hats.

clue.text: Cremation site almost at the heart of old tomb

indicators.note: almost cuts off the last letter

parts.note: a pyre is where bodies are burned
amid means in the middle of

explanation.surface: A cremation site sits almost at the centre of an ancient tomb.
explanation.definitionFit: An Egyptian monumental burial structure is an ancient tomb.

clue.text: One could use hammer for battering outlet

definitions.meaning: a carpenter is slang a woodworker who hammers
a fish-and-chip shop sells battered fish

explanation.walkthrough: A chippy is British slang both for a carpenter and for a fish-and-chip shop.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a joiner who hammers, and for a takeaway frying battered fish.

clue.text: Beginner grabbing top of leather flail

indicators.note: grabbing means one word holds the other inside

parts.note: a founder starts something, a beginner

indicators.note: top of means the first letter is taken

explanation.surface: A novice grabs the top of a leather whip.
explanation.definitionFit: To struggle clumsily, thrashing about, is to flail.

clue.text: Headdresses seen in the centre of town

indicators.note: only the central part of the word is kept, losing its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Headdresses are seen in the town centre.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to a city or town is the adjective meaning urban-like, metropolitan.

clue.text: One in singles bar may try to withdraw

definitions.text: One in singles bar may try to
definitions.meaning: to attract and pick up a partner in a bar
to retreat, as troops are drawn back

explanation.definitionFit: Slang for picking up a date, and also to draw back or retreat.

clue.text: Too soon to have left for mass in cleric's office

indicators.note: L for left replaces M for mass

explanation.surface: Someone left mass too early, in a cleric's office.
explanation.definitionFit: The rank or office held by a senior churchman, a bishop or similar.

clue.text: Men in crowd backing sweeper

indicators.note: backing means the whole is read in reverse
in places the men inside the crowd

parts.note: OR, other ranks, means soldiers or men

explanation.surface: Men in the crowd support a road sweeper.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-handled brush is used for sweeping.

clue.text: Seek delis not running out of meat

indicators.note: running suggests letters on the move, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Look for delicatessens that haven't run out of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Reduced to the bare bones, with all flesh stripped away.
